directive.thread_id: cloud job 2026-11-03: one judge for every check, reading one check list by branch
directive.quote: Turn all his checks into ONE generic check system; everything in lists, one generic process, the decision engine under it too, for any kind of thing: book, script, article, post.

job: Find a branch's ancestors nearest first, select the check rows that belong to its lineage, and build door filters for those rows.

old_copy.deleted_with: The public branch.mjs path becomes an export-only adapter to branch-core.mjs; its old implementation remains only in the inactive source-baseline artifact.

preserve: The complete branch implementation: refusal types, scalar and list link reading, one-parent checks, records-door where filters, nearest-first lineage, refusal of unknown parents and cycles, and branch check filtering.
The current public API exports and behavior; branch.mjs forwards every export to this core so existing consumers keep their entry path.
The original methodLineage history in decide-with-a-method/read-data/method.mjs and the older extends model are preserved as provenance; whole-method loading remains a separate job.
allowed_deltas: The implementation moves from branch.mjs into branch-core.mjs while its existing public module becomes a one-line export adapter.
The core header records the canonical implementation path; the complete executable implementation is retained from the inactive baseline.
banned_substitutions: A person, branch, check row, or link-field choice embedded in the implementation.
Replacing the existing lineage, refusal, list-link, or door-filter behavior with a second implementation or a weaker check.

distinct_from.why: Its original methodLineage helper selected checks for a method. That helper was extracted into the branch feature; whole-method loading and step-specific checklist composition remain in method.mjs.
The old app resolves extends while loading whole methods. The current branch implementation supplies generic lineage, row filters and records-door where shapes; those are different jobs.
